name: oauth2-4d954e69-blind29-ots
instr:
# A Go delegated-access credential library that misreports results across the board, without a test suite

The repository has received 29 separate undocumented edits. What follows is only what I watched happen while exercising the library against servers I control; none of it is theory.

Anything that has to read a private key is dead. Feeding in well-formed RSA material as PEM text, the same bytes that worked before, always comes back with a complaint that the material ought to be PEM or plain PKCS1 or PKCS8, so every flow that proves itself with such a key gives up before it ever reaches the network. With that repaired, posting a self-made assertion to an endpoint still fails: a server answering 200 with a perfectly good body is reported to me as a failed fetch, quoting the successful 200 OK reply back at me, while a server answering 400 with a problem body still produces the same structured failure it always did. Minting a self-issued credential straight from a service account key file is wrong twice over: supplying an audience and no scopes is refused outright with the message that one of the two has to be given, while supplying only scopes is accepted, and when the call is accepted, asking it for a credential hands back a failure even though the key and the claims are fine and the cryptographic proof was in fact produced. Assembling a payload of claims that already carries an explicit issued-at time fails too, with an issued-at of ten and a stated end of 3610 it insists
